sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

2. The second bail application has been filed by the applicant-accused in Case Crime No.607 of 2021,
under Sections - 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station- Rath,
District- Hamirpur with the prayer to enlarge the applicant-accused on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: The first bail application of the applicant has been dismissed for want of prosecution by this Court vide order dated 31.01.2024 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.37858 of 2022.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.37858 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: 3. It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has not committed any offence.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text:
Applicant is husband of deceased and their marriage has taken place on Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37692748/
1 15.07.2021.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: The allegations of dowry demand and harassment of deceased are wholly false.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: Only general allegations have been levelled against all the accused persons including the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: It was submitted that only four days prior to the incident, deceased was brought from her parental home and, thereafter, on the occasion of bhaiyadooj, no one has visited from her parental home, due to which, she was under depression and committed suicide.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: In this connection, statement of one Kalawati was referred.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: In postmortem report, except ligature mark, no other injury has been shown on body of deceased and cause of death has been shown asphyxia as a result of ante-mortem hanging.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: 4. It is further submitted that applicant-accused is in jail since 08.11.2021 and only part statement of one witness has been recorded so far but after that he is not appearing for his further statement.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: The trial Court has even issued non-bailable warrants against P.W. 1 but he is not been appearing for further statement.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: It was submitted that trial of the case would take sufficient long time.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text:
Lastly, it was submitted that applicant is languishing in jail since 08.11.2021, having no criminal history, and that in case the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in trial.
5.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of deceased and that deceased has suffered death other than under normal circumstances within a short period of one year of her marriage.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: 6. Considering submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of detention and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the matter, a case for bail is made out.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: 7. The bail application is allowed.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text:
8. Let the applicant - Mukesh involved in aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing each a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:
i.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text:
v. The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37692748/
2 evidence.
9.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: In case of breach of any of the above condition, the Court concerned shall be at liberty to cancel bail of applicant in accordance with law.

sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: List has been revised.

sentences.text:
2. Heard Sri Sunil Kumar Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Sunil Kumar, learned A.G.A.
for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 259 of 2021, under Sections 498A, 304B, 201 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station- Sahaswan, District- Badaun, during the pendency of trial.
4.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text:
As per prosecution story, the marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the deceased person as per Hindu Rites in the year 2016, the applicant and other family members are stated to have subjected the victim to cruelty for demand of a motorcycle and Rs. 1,00,000/- as dowry, thereby Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182802796/
1 leading her to death on 10.06.2021.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is alleged in the FIR that applicant had called the son of the informant and informed that his wife has left for his house, but when she did not reach his house till the evening of 5 PM, as such, after getting suspicion, the son of the informant-Kaptan is stated to have come to the house of the applicant and inquired about the incident and he found that applicant and family members had left the house in a hurry.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: The informant suspected that his daughter has been put to death by the applicant and his family members and her dead body has been concealed somewhere.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: He has nothing to do with the said offence.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: The FIR is delayed by about five days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: The cause of death could not be ascertained, as such, viscera was preserved and no injury was found on the body of the deceased person.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that it is a clear cut case of false implication as the dead body of the deceased person is stated to have been recovered on the pointing out of the father of the applicant, as such, applicant has nothing to do with the said offence.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: The offence, if any, may be attributed to be committed by the father of the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: 6. It is further argued by learned counsel for the applicant that there is no criminal antecedent of the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: The applicant is languishing in jail since 15.06.2021 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: 7. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the applicant absconded from his residence, and the deceased's body was recovered from the agricultural field where the applicant and his family members used to work.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: In view of this conduct, the applicant is not entitled to be granted bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: 8. This Court had called for status of trial vide order dated 01.07.2025.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text:
As per the status report,
seven witnesses have been examined and the trial is at its conclusive end.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: 9. The Supreme Court in case of X Vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr. reported in 2024 INSC 909, has held that once the trial has commenced, it should be allowed to reach to its final conclusion, which may either result in conviction or acquittal of the accused.

entities.text: X Vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr. reported in 2024 INSC 909
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: The bail should not be normally granted to the accused after the charge has been framed.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: It should also not be granted by looking into the discrepancies here or there in the deposition.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text:
10. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and considering the fact that seven witnesses have been examined and the dead body of the deceased was recovered on the pointing out of the father of the applicant from the agricultural field where the applicant his family members used to work and applicant's absence at the time of arrival of the son of the informant-Kaptan and also taking into consideration the post mortem report whereby mud was found in the trachea of the deceased person and in light of the judgment passed by Supreme Court in case of X Vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr.
(supra), I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.

entities.text: X Vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences.text: 11. The bail application is found devoid of merits and is, accordingly, rejected.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 6 August, 2025.json

sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Court No. - 65 HON'BLE SANJAY KUMAR SINGH, J.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Heard Mr. Prashant Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State and perused the record.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: By means of this bail application, applicant Mukesh, who is involved in Session Case No. 514 of 2024 arising out of Case Crime No. 381 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B, 312 IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, police station Kotwali Karvi, district Chitrakoot, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text:
As per prosecution case, in brief, complainant Ramashankar Bhujwa, who is father of the deceased,
got an F.I.R. lodged on 10.06.2024 against Mukesh (applicant), Shalini, Chunni and Anil, who are husband, sisters-in-law and brother-in-law of the deceased, respectively, stating inter alia that marriage of his daughter Ranjana was solemnized with the applicant Mukesh two years back.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text:
In the marriage, sufficient dowry and household articles were given as per his capacity but after marriage,
his daughter's in-laws started harassing in her matrimonial home and there was consistent demand of Rs. 2 lacs and 02 gold chains in dowry.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: On 02.06.2024, his daughter made a phone call that accused persons are beating her and after two days, he came to know from the uncle of the applicant that his daughter is admitted in Swaroop Rani Hospital, Prayagraj.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: When he reached there, he found that she was lying on bed with oxygen support.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is argued by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is husband of the deceased and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: General and omnibus allegations of demand of dowry have been levelled against all the accused persons, which is false and against the evidence on record.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is next submitted that in fact, at the time of incident, the deceased was having pregnancy of about 7-8 months and she had received simple head injury due to her felling from stairs.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Thereafter, she was immediately taken to District Hospital, Karvi, Chitrakoot and further she was admitted in Swaroop Rani Hopsital, Prayagraj.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The information about the said incident was given to her parents, on which they reached at the hospital and at that time, the deceased was alive and was under medical treatment.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Later on, she died on 05.06.2024.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The ward body of the hospital gave information to the police and thereafter inquest proceeding was conducted and the applicant has participated in the said proceeding and he is also one of the panch witnesses.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: After inquest proceeding, post mortem of the deceased was also conducted, in which 10 stitches wounds of 13 cm on left side of parietal to vertex region of head was found and thereafter body of the deceased was cremated by the applicant and his family members but till that time, no complaint was made by the parents of the deceased.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Later on, in order to settle his personal score, the complainant got the F.I.R. lodged after five days on 10.06.2024 and there is no plausible explanation of delay in lodging the F.I.R.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The applicant does not have any criminal history to his credit.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Lastly, it is submitted that there is no chance of the Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110189880/
2 applicant fleeing away from the judicial process or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The applicant is languishing in jail since 14.06.2024 and in case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and cooperate with the trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant reiterating the prosecution case as mentioned in the F.I.R. but does not dispute the above factual aspect of the matter as argued on behalf of the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find that before the trial Court, statement of the complainant Ramashankar has been recorded as PW-1 and from perusal of the same, it is clear that complainant's side were very much present in the hospital during the treatment of the deceased.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The complainant in his cross-examination has stated inter alia that he did not spend anything on his daughter's treatment.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: He never filed any complaint with police against his daughter's in-laws and he did not hold any panchayat in this regard.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The stairs in the house of Mukesh are cemented and have pointed edges.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The steepness of the stairs meant that anyone climbing with their eye closed could easily fall.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: From the statement of PW-1, it is also clear that injury which was found on the head of the deceased may occur on felling down from stairs.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is also not in dispute that the applicant tried his best to provide medical aid to his wife and to save her life but she could not survive, which shows natural conduct of the applicant and in-laws of the deceased, which is also one of the relevant factor for considering bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Here it is also relevant to mention that the parameters for considering the bail of accused pending trial and conviction or acquittal of accused after adducing evidences by both the parties before the trial Court are different.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: This Court is of the view that each case turns on its own facts and circumstances.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Even a little difference between the facts of two cases, may alter the entire aspect.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: In view of the provisions under Section 113B of the Evidence Act, it is not that the Courts will shut eyes and act as a silent spectator in all the cases while considering bail applications, the Courts are duty bound to consider broader aspect of the matter and in the light of nature of allegations, the relevant materials of the case diary either produced by the complainant's side or by the accused's side to prove his/her innocence cannot be ignored because bail matters are also related to the valuable liberty of the accused.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The further details relating to the incident need not be referred to herein since the allegations and the defence thereto is still open to be urged by the parties in the trial Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as well as keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused and submissions of the learned counsel for the parties,
this Court is of the opinion that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Let the applicant Mukesh be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions, which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) That the applicant shall cooperate in the expeditious disposal of the trial and shall regularly attend the court unless inevitable.
(ii) That the applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: (iii) That after his release, the applicant shall not involve in any criminal activity.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: (iv) The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: In case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs State Of U.P. on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text:

opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
The steepness of the stairs meant that anyone climbing with their eye closed could easily fall.
From the statement of PW-1, it is also clear that injury which was found on the head of the deceased may occur on felling down from stairs.
It is also not in dispute that the applicant tried his best to provide medical aid to his wife and to save her life but she could not survive, which shows natural conduct of the applicant and in-laws of the deceased, which is also one of the relevant factor for considering bail.
Here it is also relevant to mention that the parameters for considering the bail of accused pending trial and conviction or acquittal of accused after adducing evidences by both the parties before the trial Court are different.
This Court is of the view that each case turns on its own facts and circumstances.
Even a little difference between the facts of two cases, may alter the entire aspect.
In view of the provisions under Section 113B of the Evidence Act, it is not that the Courts will shut eyes and act as a silent spectator in all the cases while considering bail applications, the Courts are duty bound to consider broader aspect of the matter and in the light of nature of allegations, the relevant materials of the case diary either produced by the complainant's side or by the accused's side to prove his/her innocence cannot be ignored because bail matters are also related to the valuable liberty of the accused.
The further details relating to the incident need not be referred to herein since the allegations and the defence thereto is still open to be urged by the parties in the trial Court.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as well as keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused and submissions of the learned counsel for the parties,
this Court is of the opinion that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
